findings.summary: The in-process 401/403/200 harness proxies MVC's AuthorizeFilter rather than the host's AuthorizationMiddleware; the gap is disclosed and the host-guarded fact only confirms the policy name.
findings.detail: The host enables endpoint routing, so [Authorize] is enforced by AuthorizationMiddleware, which is not reachable without Microsoft.AspNetCore.TestHost (a disallowed new dependency). The test harness disables endpoint routing so MVC's AuthorizeFilter evaluates the same [Authorize] metadata against the same IAuthorizationService and a policy registered with the pinned host shape (authenticated principal + Administrator role claim). The 401/403 results can only arise when the filter runs and enforces, and my independent probe (replacing the gate with [AllowAnonymous]) failed exactly the 3 expected tests, so the harness is genuinely load-bearing rather than vacuous. The host-guarded fact EndpointUsesThePinnedHostAdministratorGatingPolicy compares the endpoint's policy name to the pinned host Jellyfin.Api.Controllers.PluginsController class-level policy, but it skips here (ARRTAGS_JELLYFIN_HOST_DIR unset) and, when run, confirms the policy name rather than host AuthorizationMiddleware enforcement. The worker documents both residuals in known_limitations (items 1 and 2) and does not claim the skip as a pass. This is an accepted, honestly disclosed residual; the pinned-host live matrix (section 9 of docs/planning/v1.2.md) is the correct place to exercise real host enforcement.
